entrypoints.summary: ServerTokenManager.getToken() generates the server JWT access token; the report identifies attacker acquisition of such a token as the relevant precondition.

code_slices.fixed: The audit reports generated JWTs were changed to use TOKEN_EXPIRY_AFTER, one hour after generation; the cited follow-up PR describes erroring when tokens are expired.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The report identifies this issuance code in backend-common's ServerTokenManager and describes the resulting JWT as a server access token.
code_slices.vulnerable: getToken() signs { sub: 'backstage-server' } with the signing key and algorithm HS256 but no expiration option or claim.

impact.affected_asset: Authorization represented by the server JWT access token and actions or information accessible while impersonating its victim.
impact.attacker_capability: Reuse an obtained server JWT access token without a time restriction.
impact.security_effect: Unbounded victim impersonation with potential information leakage or unauthorized actions.

causal_trace.summary: ServerTokenManager.getToken() signs an HS256 JWT whose payload contains the constant server subject.
The signing options in the reported construction omit an expiration claim, so the generated access token has no bounded temporal validity.
A previously obtained access token remains valid indefinitely and can be reused without a time restriction.
A holder of an obtained token can impersonate the victim at any time, potentially causing information leakage or other unauthorized actions.

failure.operation: Replay of a previously obtained JWT access token after any elapsed time because the token has no expiration bound.

primary_invariant.statement: Server JWT access tokens must include an expiration that bounds the period in which the bearer credential is valid.
primary_invariant.violated_because: getToken() signs the reported JWT without an expiration claim, leaving its validity indefinite.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit provides the vulnerable signing snippet, stated replay consequence, and marks remediation FULLY. The supplied PR pages establish merged remediation intent, including expiration and expired-token error handling, but do not expose complete diffs, consuming-service code, a testcase assertion, or an observed execution result. Token acquisition is a report-stated precondition rather than a demonstrated path.

remediation.invariant_restored: Generated JWTs use TOKEN_EXPIRY_AFTER, one hour after generation, and the follow-up change states that expired backend tokens fail with an error.
